cards.text: People are bringing little children to Jesus, so He'll place His hands on them. Here they come, one little one after another.

cards.question: Jesus' disciples see people bringing little children to Him. What do the disciples do?

answers.text: Rebuke the people who brought them
Line the children up for Him
Carry the children to Jesus themselves

cards.text: So the disciples have turned themselves into Jesus' security team, velvet rope and all. Then Jesus sees what they're doing.

cards.question: Jesus sees His disciples rebuking the people who brought the little children, and He is ___.

cards.text: Jesus tells them, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them!” Security team, you are OFF the clock.

cards.question: Jesus gives a reason His disciples shouldn't hinder the little children. Who does He say the kingdom of God belongs to?
Jesus says anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.
After Jesus says all this, He takes the little children in His arms, places His hands on them and blesses them.

cards.text: Jesus starts on His way, and a man comes RUNNING up and drops to his knees in front of Him. Friend, nobody runs AND kneels for small talk.

cards.question: The man kneels before Jesus and calls Him Good Teacher. What does the man ask Him?

answers.text: What he must do to inherit eternal life
Which commandment is the most important
Where Jesus will be teaching next

cards.text: Before Jesus answers, He asks one of His own: “Why do you call Me good?” Then Jesus says, “No one is good except God alone.”

cards.question: Jesus lists keeping the Sabbath holy as one of the commandments the man knows.
Jesus lists commandments like do not murder and do not steal. What does the man say back?

answers.text: He has kept all of them since his youth
He has broken most of them over the years
He has never been taught all of them

cards.text: Since his youth, he says, and friend, I can't keep my apron clean through ONE batch. Then Jesus looks at him, and loves him.

cards.question: Jesus tells the man there is one thing he lacks: go sell everything he owns and give to the ___.

cards.text: Jesus tells him he'll have treasure in heaven. Then He says, “Then come, follow Me.”

cards.question: Jesus invites the man to sell everything and follow Him. What does the man do?

answers.text: Sells it all that same day
Asks for more time to decide

cards.question: The man was saddened by Jesus' words and went away in sorrow, because he had great ___.

cards.text: The man walks away sad. Jesus looks around at His disciples and says, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!”

cards.question: The disciples are amazed when Jesus tells them how hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God.

cards.text: But Jesus speaks to them again, and this time He calls them Children: “Children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!”

cards.question: Jesus gives a picture of how hard it is for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God. What does He say is easier?

answers.text: A camel passing through the eye of a needle
A boulder floating across the Jordan River
A tower built all the way up to the sky

cards.text: A CAMEL through a NEEDLE, and friend, I can't even squeeze ONE more cookie box onto a full shelf. The disciples are even more astonished.

cards.question: The disciples are even more astonished at Jesus' camel picture. What do they ask one another?

answers.text: Why did the rich man leave

cards.question: Jesus looks at His astonished disciples and says being saved is impossible with man, but not with ___.
Jesus tells His disciples that only some things are possible with God.

cards.text: Then Peter, one of the disciples, speaks up: “Look, we have left everything and followed You.” I bet Peter is wondering where that leaves them.

cards.question: Peter says the disciples left everything to follow Jesus. Jesus says anyone who leaves home or family for His sake and the gospel will receive what in the present age?

answers.text: A hundredfold in houses and family and fields
A crown to wear on the last day
Nothing at all until the age to come

cards.question: Jesus promises that people who leave everything for Him will receive a hundredfold with no persecutions.
Jesus says the people who leave everything for Him will receive a hundredfold now, and in the age to come, eternal ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus finishes with one more line about who's first and who's last. Hold onto your apron, friend.

cards.question: Jesus finishes with a line about who is first and who is last. What does He say?

answers.text: Many who are first will be last
Many who are rich will stay first
Many who are last will stay last

findings.problem: "He asks one of His own" can easily be read as Jesus turning to ask one of His own disciples. In Mark 10:18, Jesus asks the man a question. The wording needs to make clear that He answers the man with a question of His own.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: No card sets up that Jesus points the man to the commandments (Mark 10:19). The baker is then asked whether one specific commandment, the Sabbath, is on a list they have never seen. Keeping the Sabbath is a real commandment, so a baker can't reason it in or out. The only way to answer is luck.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The card opens by retelling Mark 10:22 ("The man walks away sad") but cites only Mark 10:23.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The question asks what is received "in the present age." That rules out both wrong answers: "A crown to wear on the last day" isn't in the present age, and "Nothing at all until the age to come" contradicts the question itself. Only the right answer fits.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card says the promise is for "people who leave everything for Him." In Mark 10:29–30, Jesus promises it to anyone who has left home or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for His sake and for the gospel. "Everything" was Peter's word (Mark 10:28), not Jesus' condition, so the card stretches the text.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The card again says "the people who leave everything for Him." Mark 10:29 names leaving home or family or fields for His sake and for the gospel, not everything.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers use "will stay," and the right answer is the only one without it, so the right answer stands out as the odd one. "Many who are rich will stay first" is also ruled out by everything Jesus just said about the rich (Mark 10:23–25).

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: Stop 2 has almost no laughs. Cards 1, 3, 9 and 13 are plain retelling, and the one joke (card 5, the cookie box on a full shelf) is mild. The stop reads like a nice dad being pleasant, not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. … If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: "I bet Peter is wondering where that leaves them" is marked as Papa Dorin's guess. But it guesses at what Peter is thinking in a way that suggests why he spoke up, and Mark 10:28 gives no reason.
findings.question: Is a marked guess ("I bet") about what someone is thinking allowed when it also suggests their reason for speaking? Or does the rule against adding reasons apply even when the guess is marked as his own?
